nodes.label: CGTK Digital Experience Platform Backend API
nodes.author: Rafly Pratama Hudzaifah Al Syahbani

nodes.label: Zero Monthly Cost Budget Constraint (Rp 100,000 total)
nodes.rationale: The entire project budget is Rp 100,000 in total, not per month. This single constraint drives nearly every stack and design decision; Render (sleeps), Railway (Hobby credit is not a price, Postgres pushes it to $10-18/month, over the whole budget) and MySQL were rejected against it.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Workers Runtime
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it has no cold start. A platform that sleeps after 15 minutes idle wakes in ~50 seconds, which is survivable on a website but fatal with a queue of students at a session gate.

nodes.label: Hono Web Framework
nodes.rationale: Small, Web-standard, runs natively on Workers so no Node compatibility shims sit in the request path.

nodes.label: Supabase (PostgreSQL, Auth, Storage)
nodes.rationale: Free tier covers ~500 participants and 250-300 concurrent with headroom, and bundles Google sign-in plus file storage that would each otherwise be a week of work. JSONB carries the admin-defined registration form.

nodes.label: supabase-js over PostgREST HTTP
nodes.rationale: Workers have no long-lived TCP sockets. PostgREST over HTTPS means there is no connection pool to exhaust when 300 phones sync at once.

nodes.label: Polling Instead of Supabase Realtime
nodes.rationale: The free tier caps Realtime at 200 concurrent connections against an expected peak of 250-300, and connection 201 fails silently: announcements would simply not arrive with nothing in any log to explain it. Announcements are polled every 30s and answer 204 when there is nothing new.

nodes.label: Zod Validation at the Module Edge
nodes.rationale: Every request body is validated at the edge of the module so nothing unvalidated ever reaches a SQL function.

nodes.label: Row Level Security (0011_rls.sql)
nodes.rationale: RLS denies the public anon key everything except a short list of genuinely public tables, so no browser ever needs to hold a database credential.

nodes.label: Worker as Sole Database Client
nodes.rationale: The Worker is the only thing that talks to the database; the service role key never leaves it because that key bypasses RLS entirely.

nodes.label: Multi-Table Operations in PostgreSQL Functions
nodes.rationale: Over HTTP, 'record the scan, add the XP, write the audit row' would be three independent calls; a dropped connection between them would award XP for a check-in that does not exist, or record attendance that never earned anything. Inside a PostgreSQL function it is one transaction (db/migrations/0008_functions.sql).

nodes.label: QR Identity (build, verify, hash)
nodes.rationale: HMAC-signed with QR_SIGNING_SECRET; rotating that secret invalidates every issued badge. Nothing in the verification path may throw because a scanner receives whatever the camera decodes, including partial reads, and a crashed scanner stops the queue.

nodes.label: Local HS256 JWT Verification with WebCrypto
nodes.rationale: Supabase access tokens are verified locally rather than by calling Supabase, because a network round trip per scan would be the slowest part of the check-in path.

nodes.label: Unified Response Envelope (sukses/data/error)
nodes.rationale: One envelope for every endpoint. 'pesan' is written in Indonesian for the person holding the phone and is displayed verbatim by the frontend; 'kode' is what code should branch on.

nodes.label: Error Code Catalog (lib/errors.ts, ~45 codes)
nodes.rationale: Messages are written for field staff, and the central error handler never leaks internals. Anything a user can trigger must have a matching code here.

nodes.label: One Module Owns One Route Prefix
nodes.rationale: Administrative routes are nested under their own module (/payments/admin/... not /admin/payments/...) so one file owns one prefix and a permission mistake cannot spread outside it.

nodes.label: Dual Mounting at Root and /api/v1
nodes.rationale: Every route answers both at the root and under /api/v1 because /api/v1 is the base URL the API Contract gives the frontend team. Same router, two spellings.

nodes.label: KV Fixed-Window Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Only active when a KV namespace is bound: 10/min auth, 30/min scanning, 5/min sync, 10/min public status lookups, 120/min otherwise.

nodes.label: Anti-Farming Keyed on (participant_id, booth_id)
nodes.rationale: Never keyed on campus_id: in Event 3 a single table is staffed by alumni from several universities at once, so a campus key would let a participant collect XP from each of them without moving. Keyed on the booth, both event formats are covered by one rule.

nodes.label: Two Booth Types in One Table (KAMPUS / JURUSAN)
nodes.rationale: booth_type is KAMPUS (Event 2, one booth per university) or JURUSAN (Event 3, one booth per major), with a CHECK constraint requiring exactly one of university_id / major_id. Alumni are placed into the right booth automatically from the active event so they never choose.

nodes.label: Booth Poster Check-In Grants No XP
nodes.rationale: Participants scan a printed poster only to unlock DI_BOOTH material. If it awarded points, photographing the poster would earn XP for someone who never attended; XP comes only from an alumnus scanning the participant.

nodes.label: Sessions Gated by Status Switch, Not Clock Time
nodes.rationale: A twenty-minute delay is normal at a school event; a time-based gate would close the scanners mid-queue. DRAFT/ACTIVE/CLOSED is the only thing that opens a scanner.

nodes.label: Append-Only XP Ledger
nodes.rationale: A reversal is a new negative row. Level is computed from the ledger and never stored, so cancelling a visit corrects the level automatically. XP ceilings are re-checked server-side because a limit enforced only on the phone is not a limit.

nodes.label: Payment Handled Entirely Outside the Platform
nodes.rationale: Administration collects cash or transfers and keeps their own book. No amount is stored anywhere, only who marked a registration settled and when, because a second set of figures here would eventually disagree with theirs.

nodes.label: Gated Payment Redirect (GET /payments/buka)
nodes.rationale: link_pembayaran and prefill_entry_id are never serialized into a participant-facing response. The form is reachable only through a server-side 302 issued after the profile is verified complete, with the registration code pre-filled, which makes forwarding the link self-defeating since a friend's payment would land under the sharer's code.

nodes.label: Offline Sync Answers 200 to Duplicates
nodes.rationale: A phone that already delivered a scan and lost the response will retry; an error status makes it retry forever while a success ends the loop. Genuine rejections are recorded in sync_conflicts for committee review. Offline scanner payloads ship token_hash, never a raw QR token, so a stolen staff phone carries nothing that can mint a working badge.

nodes.label: Minor-Participant Privacy Rules
nodes.rationale: Participants are minors. Alumni see only participants who ticked the consent box and never a phone number; liaison officers see aggregate counts only. quiz_options.bobot (the answer key) is never sent to a client.

nodes.label: Audit Logging via catat_audit
nodes.rationale: Every privileged mutation writes to audit_logs. Reversing a payment is Super Admin only, requires a written reason, and revokes the QR identity.

nodes.label: Form Fields Deactivated, Never Deleted
nodes.rationale: Deleting a form field orphans the answers already submitted under it.

nodes.label: Nothing a Division Might Change Lives in Code
nodes.rationale: Ticket wording, XP values, schedules, FAQ text, announcements, sponsors and form questions all live in the database so they can be changed from the admin dashboard without a deployment.

nodes.label: Economy Mode (mode_hemat)
nodes.rationale: Slows leaderboard and announcement polling and hides alumni statistics, but scanning, attendance and XP are never disabled.

nodes.label: Leaderboard Freeze
nodes.rationale: Locks the ranking before the ceremony so the winners cannot change mid-announcement. Ranking also carries tie-breakers, winner confirmation and an anomaly check (0009_leaderboard.sql).

nodes.label: Health Check Deliberately Touches the Database
nodes.rationale: A health check that only proves the Worker is running would report green while every check-in fails.

nodes.label: Registration Code Alphabet Excludes 0 O 1 I L
nodes.rationale: The code is read aloud across a desk and typed on a phone, and those are the characters that go wrong.

nodes.label: One Transaction per Migration File
nodes.rationale: 39 tables across eleven files applied in filename order and recorded in _migrations; each file runs in its own transaction so a failure leaves the database at the last complete migration rather than half-applied.

nodes.label: Migrations Require Direct Port 5432
nodes.rationale: DATABASE_URL must use the direct port 5432 and never the pooler port 6543; the migration runner refuses it.

nodes.label: Demo Data (db:contoh) Deliberately Not a Migration
nodes.rationale: Fills events, sessions, universities, majors, university_majors, booths and sponsors with plausible rows so the frontend has something to render before the event division supplies real data. It is not a migration on purpose: demo rows must not reappear every time the database is rebuilt.

nodes.label: Per-Module Why Comments as Design Record
nodes.rationale: Every module file opens with a comment explaining why it works the way it does, not what the code says; those comments are the design record and must be kept current when behaviour changes.

nodes.label: Schema-Pinning Test Suite (tests/skema.test.ts)
nodes.rationale: Reads the migration SQL and asserts the domain decisions are still in it, because they are the decisions easiest to undo by accident. Both suites run without a database.

nodes.label: Load Test Scenario 7: Simultaneous Offline Queue Flush
nodes.rationale: Nine scenarios at 200 concurrent users, to be run no later than two weeks before the event; the scenario most worth attention is every phone flushing its offline queue at once when venue signal returns.

nodes.label: No Automatic Backups on Supabase Free Tier
nodes.rationale: A daily dump is required because restoring from a backup that was never taken is not a recovery plan.

nodes.label: Frontend PWA on Cloudflare Pages (separate ownership)
nodes.rationale: Frontend, quiz engine, achievements, missions and the leaderboard UI are owned by other Web subdivision members. The leaderboard reads the XP ledger and never writes to it; that boundary is what keeps two people out of the same table. Same-origin deployment also means no CORS in production.

nodes.label: Same-Origin Deployment Removes CORS
nodes.rationale: Pages and Workers share an origin, so ALLOWED_ORIGINS unset in production means same-origin only.
